synopsis: Randomized trials found that hypothesis-driven management increased rational termination of projects or courses of action [f9448, f16378, f9682]. Chapter 12 describes the evidence as one trial followed by four more involving 759 firms [f9448]. It identifies the trials as start-up research from an adjacent domain, so the reported support is not direct evidence from heavy off-road collision-mitigation development [f10128]. The glossary restates the positive finding without that domain qualification [f16378, f10128].

relations.note: Both report increased rational termination in randomized trials; Chapter 12 adds trial counts.
Projects and courses of action express the same reported termination outcome.
Identifies start-ups as the evidence domain and qualifies its relevance as adjacent.
Restates the positive trial finding with additional trial and firm counts.
Both report randomized-trial support for increased rational termination.
Adds the trial sequence and 759-firm count to the randomized-trial evidence.
